data.narrative:
Helios is a Series A climate and energy company that has raised $26M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a narrow peer universe comprising one public company (LNZA) and eight private firms in the climate and energy sector, including comparable-stage players such as Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix.

A stage-progression methodology was applied, using the $26M in total capital raised as a baseline valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage advancement. This approach yields an implied valuation of $52M. A peer-median comparison was not applicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the Climate & Energy sector—while eight peers operate in this space, none met the threshold of three or more datapoints when filtered for stage and valuation tier similarity. Relying on an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable bias.

The triangulated valuation range is $44M to $60M, with a median point of $52M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty given the limited comparable dataset and the absence of traditional peer benchmarking. Key sensitivities include actual exit multiples achieved by similar-stage climate tech companies and market conditions at Helios's next fundraising event. The range should be treated as indicative rather than definitive pending access to a richer peer dataset or additional company-specific financial metrics.
